key_insight: A simple “deletions” strategy is the most effective way to extract local atomic environments from large simulations for use in small periodic DFT reference calculations.
engineering_relevance: This helps make active learning and on-the-fly training of interatomic potentials more practical by reliably converting huge atomistic models into DFT-ready fragments.
method: Benchmarked multiple ways to cut out atomic environments from bulk simulations.
Tested extraction and embedding schemes for periodic-boundary DFT calculations, including passivation needs.
Compared methods across diverse systems: amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark study over several material systems, with deletions outperforming the alternative extraction methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the extracted fragment and any passivating envelope preserve the local chemistry and boundary conditions of the target environment.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
